quarterly_data.signal: Q4 2025 revenue came in above the high end of guidance at $7.3 million, down from $10.1 million in Q3, as Navitas deprioritized low-power China mobile/consumer business and cut back its distribution network. For the first time, high-power markets were the majority of quarterly revenue, and mobile fell from a majority of revenue in Q3 to less than 25% in Q4. Management said it believes Q4 was the revenue bottom. Full-year 2025 revenue was $45.9 million, versus $83.3 million in 2024.
quarterly_data.figure: Q4 rev $7.3 million (Q3 $10.1 million); mobile less than 25%; FY2025 rev $45.9 million vs $83.3 million

quarterly_data.signal: Q1 2026 guidance: revenue of $8 million to $8.5 million, the first quarter-over-quarter growth since the pivot, with gross margin of 38.7% plus or minus 25 basis points and operating expenses of approximately $15 million. Management expects sequential growth to continue throughout 2026 on high-power demand, with opex held flat. It expects mobile to 'become insignificant by the end of '26'. The CFO said margins should start expanding again 'in Q2 and beyond', helped by mix, scale and new package suppliers that are ramping to cut costs.
quarterly_data.figure: Q1 guide between $8 million and $8.5 million; GM 38.7%; opex approximately $15 million

quarterly_data.signal: 800V HVDC timing and the GaN-vs-SiC split: Navitas is working with multiple hyperscalers on 800-volt HVDC adoption. The CEO said the step function is 'really about '27', tied to the Kyber rack, as megawatt racks force high-voltage GaN to replace silicon on the primary side. GaN may appear earlier in 48-volt IBC. Before that, demand for classic AC-DC PSUs is driving SiC (1.2 kV) growth 'throughout '26'. The CEO said hyperscalers are pulling GaN onto the 800V primary side, and Navitas has not seen any significant SiC primary-side use. Designs run through PSU OEMs/ODMs in Taiwan, China and the U.S. and through merchant power companies.

Product sampling: 100-volt and 650-volt GaN samples for AI data centers (800-volt HVDC and 48-volt IBC) are being evaluated by more than a dozen customers. On February 9 Navitas announced an all-GaN 10-kilowatt 800-volt to 50-volt DC-DC platform with 98.5% peak efficiency that supports the plus or minus 400-volt VDC standard. It was co-developed with a leading customer and serves as a reference design only; Navitas does not plan to sell the modules. Navitas is also sampling its first 1.2 kV Gen 5 SiC product (topside-cooled Q-DPAK) to multiple OEMs and ODMs designing AI data center AC-DC PSUs.
quarterly_data.figure: 10-kilowatt 800-volt to 50-volt GaN DC-DC; 98.5% peak efficiency; more than a dozen customers evaluating

quarterly_data.signal: Grid/SST opportunity: sampling of the 2.3 kV and 3.3 kV ultra-high-voltage SiC modules has been accelerated, and more than 15 OEMs (mostly U.S. and Europe) are evaluating them for solid-state transformers, battery energy storage, megawatt chargers and solar. Design cycles are longer, but the CEO expects 'significant revenue growth starting '27'. Content sizing: $25,000 to $35,000 per megawatt of total Navitas SAM content, of which $10,000 to $12,000 is outside the data center (SST, BESS).
quarterly_data.figure: $25,000 to $35,000 per megawatt total; $10,000 to $12,000 outside data center; over 15 OEMs evaluating

quarterly_data.signal: Competition: the 800-volt AI factory ecosystem list is 'up to 13 vendors', but few of them offer both high/mid-voltage GaN and high-voltage SiC. The CEO named Infineon as the competitor Navitas meets most often. Navitas holds a cross-license with Infineon and said it does not rely on Infineon for its wins. He said circuit protection is a possible future addition to the product line as data-center voltages rise.

Performance computing: more than 15 projects are in production and about twice that many are in design, covering high-power chargers and power units from 170-watt up to 360 watts for leading global computing companies. Management expects momentum to continue through 2026.
quarterly_data.figure: more than 15 projects in production; approximately twice that number in designing

quarterly_data.signal: Navitas 2.0 restructuring: distribution partners were consolidated from approximately 40 to less than 10, and headcount was cut 19% in Q4 while the company hired for U.S. high-power markets. Q4 GAAP results included a $16.6 million restructuring and impairment charge. A November private placement brought net proceeds of approximately $96 million, and quarter-end cash was $237 million with no debt. The CEO also announced that CFO Todd Glickman is stepping down.
quarterly_data.figure: distributors approximately 40 to less than 10; 19% headcount cut; $16.6 million charge; cash $237 million

contracts.signal: Navitas CEO: on November 20 Navitas announced a long-term strategic technology and manufacturing partnership with GlobalFoundries for U.S. GaN design and manufacturing, which also opens critical and national security applications. Development began 'a few weeks ago'. Production is expected to begin 'later in the year' and accelerate in 2027, with a later move to 8-inch wafers to lower costs and add scale.
contracts.date_signed: November 20 (announcement); production later in the year, accelerating in 2027
